blocks.text: Tom was the youngest member of the town's tree-planting club, and he mostly listened during planning meetings. Last autumn, half of the young trees the club planted along the river died within weeks. The older members thought the soil was too poor and wanted to buy expensive fertiliser. Tom, who walked along the river every morning, had noticed that the dead trees were all on the side where people let their dogs run. He suggested putting up simple wooden fences instead. The club tried his idea on twenty new trees, and every one of them survived the winter. At the spring meeting, the chairwoman asked Tom to lead the next planting day.
1. Why did many young trees die?
A. The soil had no fertiliser.    B. Dogs damaged them on one side of the river.    C. The winter was too cold.    D. They were planted too late.
2. What can we infer about Tom?
A. He noticed things others missed.    B. He knew a lot about fertiliser.    C. He owned several dogs.    D. He disliked meetings.
3. Why did the chairwoman ask Tom to lead the next planting day?
A. He was the oldest member.    B. His idea had proved effective.    C. He had bought the fences.    D. He asked for the job.
